scope:
Package FLAKE-1 (WEB, small, a real app bug the owner can hit on a slow phone): a late popstate closes a layer that was opened AFTER our own history.back(). Evidence (parallel session S2, android-smoke emulator runs on 3 phone profiles, twice now): after '⋮ > Ustawienia' the settings panel does not stay open - the screen at timeout is the chat root ('☰ New conversation ... ⋮ A provider key is needed'), at RANDOM steps and RANDOM profiles (Gate 0 step 5 'Wstecz' on pixel_6 1.0 in one run, step 4 'Modele > Role' on pixel_5 and step 5 'Wstecz' on pixel_6 1.3 in the next); the driver click is a JS element.click() right after m1Reset = up to 8 x window.__loomBack() in a row, so animation is not the cause. S2's hypotheses: a click goes to a menu that is closing, or the panel opens and closes immediately. Branch claude/m1-w0 is at b1b34f17 or later.
MY STATIC ANALYSIS (verify, do not trust): loom/web/src/shell/history.ts LayerStack. back() closes the topmost layer synchronously and reconcile() issues host.back() = history.back(), which is ASYNCHRONOUS, and sets pendingSince = now; popped(depth) treats the next popstate as 'our own' ONLY while pendingSince !== null. reconcile() clears pendingSince after backTimeoutMs (preset BACK_TIMEOUT_PRESET_MS = 1000 ms: 'the back never arrived'). A SPEED ASSUMPTION: on a loaded emulator/WebView the popstate of an earlier own back can arrive later than 1 s; meanwhile the app opens a new layer (the ⋮ menu, then the settings panel - the stack pushes/reuses an entry), reconcile() has dropped pendingSince, and the LATE popstate then reaches popped() with pendingSince === null, is read as the person's Back and closes every layer above its depth - the menu or the freshly opened panel disappears. Several quick back() calls (m1Reset) also create several in-flight own backs of which only ONE is remembered (reconcile returns early while pendingSince is fresh, so the second layer closed shares the first wait). Check both.
DO: (1) REPRODUCE FIRST as a unit test with the existing fake-host pattern (loom/web/tests/shell/ - find the history test via `grep -rl LayerStack loom/web/tests`, npm script test:shell-history or similar): a host whose popstate delivery you control; sequence: open menu + panel, back() twice quickly (the m1Reset shape), advance the clock beyond backTimeoutMs WITHOUT delivering the popstates, open a new layer (menu, then panel), THEN deliver the late popstates: assert the new layers must stay open (today they close = the test fails). Also a variant: two in-flight own backs, only the first answered in time. (2) FIX in LayerStack without a speed assumption: remember EVERY in-flight own back (a count or a list of the depths they will land on) and classify a popstate by what it is, not by how long ago we asked: a popstate whose depth matches an expected landing depth of one of our own pending backs is ours and is only consumed, however late; the timeout stays ONLY as the safety net for a back that never answers (nothing behind the entry) and must not turn a late own popstate into a user Back - decide how (e.g. keep an expired expectation 'weakly' so a matching depth after expiry is still treated as ours while no user-visible layer would be wrongly kept; or drop the time based expiry and use the depth sequence); the person's own Back (browser/Android Back, a popstate that matches no expectation) must still close layers exactly as before - keep every existing test green and add the cases. Make the policy configurable/data where the file already has an options object (backTimeoutMs stays an option; say what the new defaults are and why). (3) APP-LEVEL REGRESSION: add a browser e2e step (390x844 touch, real loom-server like the neighbours, e.g. in e2e/m1-navigator-native.mjs or a new e2e/m1-history-native.mjs with npm script and CI step in .github/workflows/loom.yml next to the neighbours) that in a loop (30 iterations) does exactly the driver's shape: m1Reset = window.__loomBack() up to 8 times, then click shell-menu-toggle, click shell-menu-settings, wait for the panel and the groups (testid shum-groups), assert it STAYS open for 1.5 s (poll, not sleep-and-read), then back; to make the race reachable on a fast desktop add a test-only way to delay popstate delivery (e.g. page.addInitScript wrapping history.back to dispatch its popstate after a configurable delay of 1500 ms via setTimeout on the original) - the step must FAIL on the old history.ts and PASS on the fixed one (prove it: run it once against `git stash`ed/old code or say how you checked). Timing rule: wait for conditions, never read an attribute right after a tap if the UI sets it from an effect. (4) Tell in the card whether the same shape can affect OTHER layers (sheets, cards, navigator path) - they share the stack, so list what the fix covers.
Words: none expected (no owner text). If a pack/word changes, regenerate builtin.inc and loom/web/src/onboarding/generated/*.json with gen_onboarding_pack.py (explicit chunk lengths) and run python3 /home/user/chatadhd/tools/clang_inc_check.py loom/build/dev. No kernel, no loom/android/smoke/* (S2 owns the driver), no new route literal. Record the decision and how to reverse it under 'S1 / M1-FLAKE1' in docs/reports/INDEX.md. Commit in 2-3 pieces (test that fails -> fix -> e2e + CI step) and push to origin claude/m1-w0. If after about 50 tool calls a piece is unfinished, commit what is consistent and return done=false with exactly what is left.
accept: cd loom/web && npm run build succeeds; the history/shell unit tests (test:shell-history or the one you find, test:shell, test:shell-menu, test:navigator-state) pass including the new cases, and the new unit test is shown FAILING on the old history.ts (paste the failing assertion) before the fix; the new e2e loop passes TWICE in a row with the delay shim on, and fails on the old code (paste how you showed it); e2e/m1-navigator-native.mjs, m1-context-sent-native.mjs and m1-context-menu-native.mjs still pass with git status clean afterwards (screenshots to a scratch M1_SHOTS_DIR); testids documented if you add any (npm run test:testids-doc); pushed to origin claude/m1-w0. The card pastes: the failing and passing unit assertions, the e2e loop result, the new backTimeout policy in words, and what other layers are covered.
rules_extra: Shared machine: never kill processes by name; record the pid/port of the e2e servers you start and kill only those. Do NOT run the full gate (S1 does). CACHE RULE: no single tool call longer than ~4 minutes - run builds, tests and e2e in the background and poll with short calls. One native build at a time (loom/build/dev of this worktree) - this package should need no native rebuild unless a pack word changes. Keep context small: grep and line ranges, never dump big files. Tests must not depend on speed or order: this package exists to remove one such dependency - do not add another (no sleeps that race; use fake clocks in unit tests, conditions in e2e). Private data: synthetic data only; never read docs/exports or eval/real-holdout-key. Nothing described as working that is only planned.
